failure_mode: L2 (abbreviation expansion). Pure short-form query: the only disease token is the bare code 'NSCLC'. A system that does not expand NSCLC -> non-small cell lung cancer/carcinoma will miss the many lung adenocarcinoma/squamous datasets that never spell out the acronym, and will fail to attach the lung (UBERON:0002048) / MONDO:0005233 facet.
pass_criteria: Top results are lung non-small cell carcinoma single-cell datasets (adenocarcinoma or squamous histology); disease facet resolves to MONDO:0005233 and tissue to lung even though the query never spells out 'lung' or 'carcinoma'.

failure_mode: L2 (two stacked abbreviations in one query). 'HCC' (disease, must expand to hepatocellular carcinoma -> liver/MONDO:0007256) AND 'PBMC' (sample type, must expand to peripheral blood mononuclear cells -> blood). The trap: systems often resolve PBMC to a liver/tumor tissue facet by proximity to HCC, or treat HCC as 'head and neck' / 'hydroxychloroquine'. Sample is BLOOD, disease is LIVER cancer; both facets must coexist correctly.
pass_criteria: Returns single-cell datasets of peripheral blood (not liver tumor tissue) drawn from hepatocellular carcinoma patients. Disease facet = MONDO:0007256 (liver), sample/tissue facet = peripheral blood, with PBMC NOT mis-mapped to liver tissue.

failure_mode: L2 (abbreviation expansion with implicit receptor semantics). 'TNBC' must expand to triple-negative breast cancer (ER-/PR-/HER2-negative breast carcinoma -> breast/MONDO:0005494). A naive system indexes datasets described only as 'ER-negative PR-negative HER2-negative breast cancer' and never as 'TNBC', so without expansion recall collapses; it must also bind the breast (UBERON:0000310) tissue facet that the bare code never states.
pass_criteria: Top results are triple-negative (ER/PR/HER2-negative) breast carcinoma single-cell datasets, including those that spell out the receptor status instead of 'TNBC'. Disease facet resolves to MONDO:0005494 and tissue to breast.

failure_mode: L2 (abbreviation expansion; non-cancer ILD). 'IPF' must expand to idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (-> lung/MONDO:0800504). Trap 1: IPF is rarely spelled out in dataset titles, hurting recall without expansion. Trap 2: IPF can be confused with 'interstitial pulmonary fibrosis' (broader ILD) or non-medical IPF; the system must keep it to the idiopathic UIP-pattern disease and bind the lung facet that the code omits.
pass_criteria: Returns single-nucleus / single-cell datasets of fibrotic human lung from idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (UIP pattern), not generic interstitial lung disease unrelated to IPF. Disease facet = MONDO:0800504, tissue = lung.

failure_mode: L2 (abbreviation expansion). 'COPD' must expand to chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (-> lung/MONDO:0005002). Datasets are frequently described via constituent phenotypes ('emphysema', 'chronic bronchitis') rather than the acronym, so without expansion + synonym bridging recall drops. The bare code also carries no tissue token, so the lung (UBERON:0002048) facet must be inferred.
pass_criteria: Top results are bulk RNA-seq of human lung from chronic obstructive pulmonary disease cohorts (including emphysema / chronic bronchitis phenotypes). Disease facet = MONDO:0005002, tissue = lung.

abbrev_under_test: NAFLD=non-alcoholic fatty liver disease;MASLD=metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease
failure_mode: L2 (abbreviation expansion + nomenclature change). The query mixes the old code 'NAFLD' and the 2023 renamed code 'MASLD' for the SAME disease (-> liver/MONDO:0013209). A good system must recognize NAFLD and MASLD as synonyms (and bridge to 'NASH', 'fatty liver', 'hepatic steatosis') so that older datasets tagged NAFLD and newer ones tagged MASLD are both retrieved; otherwise the corpus splits across the rename and recall is halved. Liver (UBERON:0002107) facet is implicit.
pass_criteria: Returns liver RNA-seq datasets for fatty liver disease regardless of whether they use the legacy 'NAFLD' or the current 'MASLD' label (and related NASH/steatosis terms). Disease facet collapses NAFLD and MASLD to MONDO:0013209, tissue = liver.

abbrev_under_test: CESC=cervical squamous cell carcinoma and endocervical adenocarcinoma
failure_mode: L2 TCGA code: 'CESC' is the exact gap a colleague hit. The bare 4-letter code is never spelled out, so unless the system expands CESC -> cervical squamous cell carcinoma / endocervical adenocarcinoma, BM25 and dense retrieval both miss every dataset that only says 'cervical cancer' or 'cervical squamous cell carcinoma'. Extra trap: CESC also dilutes into generic 'cervical' tokens.
pass_criteria: Top results are scRNA-seq studies of cervical (squamous cell / endocervical) carcinoma; system must demonstrably expand CESC to cervical cancer rather than treating it as an opaque token.

failure_mode: L2 TCGA code: 'THCA' must expand to thyroid carcinoma. Without expansion the system gets zero lexical overlap with 'thyroid cancer' datasets. Secondary trap: THCA visually collides with THC-A (tetrahydrocannabinolic acid) in chemistry/metabolomics corpora, so a naive embedder may pull cannabinoid studies.
pass_criteria: Top results are methylation studies of thyroid carcinoma (ideally tumor-vs-normal); no cannabinoid/THC chemistry hits in top-10.

failure_mode: L2 TCGA code: 'SARC' is one of the exact codes a colleague hit (CESC/THCA/SARC). It must expand to the sarcoma umbrella AND understand that subtype names (leiomyosarcoma, liposarcoma) are members of it. Trap: SARC is also a common gene/protein abbreviation (e.g. SARC sarco- prefixes, SARS coronavirus near-collision) so it can be mis-tokenized.
pass_criteria: Top results are sarcoma (soft-tissue, leiomyosarcoma/liposarcoma) transcriptomics; the code SARC is expanded to the sarcoma family rather than treated as noise or confused with SARS.

failure_mode: L2 + the headline BRCA-code-vs-BRCA-gene trap: here 'BRCA' is the TCGA cohort code for breast invasive carcinoma, NOT the BRCA1/BRCA2 tumor-suppressor genes. Systems that key on the gene meaning will surface germline-mutation/hereditary breast-ovarian studies and miss the breast-carcinoma transcriptomic cohort. The query context ('tumor cohort', 'breast carcinoma TCGA project', explicit 'not BRCA1/BRCA2') must drive disambiguation toward the disease cohort.
pass_criteria: Top results are breast carcinoma cohort RNA-seq (TCGA-BRCA-style); top-10 must NOT be dominated by BRCA1/BRCA2 germline-mutation gene studies and must avoid the forbidden substrings.

abbrev_under_test: LUAD=lung adenocarcinoma;LUSC=lung squamous cell carcinoma;COAD=colon adenocarcinoma;PRAD=prostate adenocarcinoma
failure_mode: L2 + L5 cardinality: four TCGA codes at once must ALL be expanded (LUAD/LUSC/COAD/PRAD) and the pan-cancer intent means results should jointly cover these four distinct carcinomas, not collapse to whichever code happens to embed strongest (LUAD usually dominates). Trap: LUSC vs LUAD are one letter apart and frequently conflated into generic 'lung cancer'; COAD/PRAD get dropped entirely if only the first code is expanded.
pass_criteria: All four codes expanded to their carcinomas; top results collectively span lung adeno, lung squamous, colon adeno, and prostate adeno scRNA-seq rather than only lung.

failure_mode: L3 ambiguous abbreviation: 'AD' = Alzheimer's disease vs atopic dermatitis. Disambiguating context here (hippocampus, amyloid-beta, tau, aged brain, snRNA-seq) forces the NEUROLOGICAL sense. Trap: system may expand AD to atopic dermatitis and return skin/eczema datasets, or leave AD unexpanded and miss Alzheimer-tagged records that never spell out the abbreviation. Contrast partner: ambig_ad_atopic.
pass_criteria: Top results are Alzheimer's-disease brain/hippocampus single-nucleus datasets (MONDO:0004975). Must NOT surface atopic-dermatitis/skin datasets despite the shared 'AD' token.

failure_mode: L3 ambiguous abbreviation: 'AD' = atopic dermatitis vs Alzheimer's disease. Disambiguating context (lesional skin biopsy, skin barrier, filaggrin, eczema) forces the DERMATOLOGY sense. Trap: 'AD' is far more frequently expanded to Alzheimer's in neuro-heavy corpora, so the system may return brain datasets. Contrast partner: ambig_ad_alzheimer.
pass_criteria: Top results are atopic-dermatitis lesional-skin RNA-seq datasets (MONDO:0011292, UBERON:0002097). Must NOT surface Alzheimer's/brain/hippocampus datasets.

failure_mode: L3 ambiguous abbreviation: 'MS' = multiple sclerosis (disease) vs mass spectrometry (a proteomics MODALITY). Disambiguating context (relapsing-remitting, demyelinating, CSF, white-matter lesions, scRNA-seq) forces the DISEASE sense. Trap: system may collapse MS to a mass-spec modality filter and return proteomics datasets, or mix the two senses. Contrast partner: ambig_ms_proteomics.
pass_criteria: Top results are multiple-sclerosis CSF/immune single-cell datasets (MONDO:0005301). Modality must remain transcriptomic (scRNA-seq), NOT mass-spectrometry proteomics.

failure_mode: L3 ambiguous abbreviation: 'MS' = mass spectrometry (proteomics modality) vs multiple sclerosis (disease). Context (LC-MS/MS, plasma proteomics, label-free quantification) forces the MASS-SPECTROMETRY/proteomics sense. Trap: a disease-biased expander may inject 'multiple sclerosis' and return MS-patient datasets. must_not_contain guards against the neurological sense leaking in. Contrast partner: ambig_ms_disease.
pass_criteria: Top results are mass-spectrometry plasma proteomics datasets (modality=proteomics). Must NOT contain multiple-sclerosis / demyelinating-disease datasets.

failure_mode: L3 ambiguous abbreviation: 'CD' = Crohn's disease vs cluster-of-differentiation marker (CD4/CD8/CD45 → cell-type facet). Context (inflamed ileal mucosa, transmural inflammation, granuloma) forces the DISEASE sense. Trap: tokenizer may read 'CD' as a generic CD-marker and route to a cell-type filter, or fail to expand to Crohn's. Contrast partner: ambig_cd_marker.
pass_criteria: Top results are Crohn's-disease intestinal-mucosa single-cell datasets (MONDO:0005011). Must NOT be driven by a generic CD-surface-marker interpretation.

failure_mode: L3 ambiguous abbreviation: 'CD' (in CD8) = cluster-of-differentiation surface marker → cell-type facet, vs Crohn's disease. Context (sorted CD8-positive cytotoxic T cells, CITE-seq surface marker panel, healthy donor) forces the MARKER/cell-type sense. Trap: a disease-biased expander may read 'CD' as Crohn's and return IBD gut datasets. must_not_contain guards against the disease sense. Contrast partner: ambig_cd_crohn.
pass_criteria: Top results are healthy-donor CD8 T-cell CITE-seq datasets (cell_type CL:0000794). Must NOT contain Crohn's/colitis/ileum datasets.

failure_mode: L4 treatment-naive exclusion: 'treatment-naive' shares tokens with 'treatment', so dense retrieval pulls in treated/neoadjuvant/post-therapy NSCLC cohorts. System must EXCLUDE any dataset where tumors were exposed to chemo/radio/immunotherapy before sampling, not just match on 'NSCLC RNA-seq'.
pass_criteria: top-5 are all NSCLC bulk RNA-seq where tumors are explicitly treatment-naive/chemo-naive at sampling; ZERO results describe neoadjuvant, post-treatment, relapsed/refractory, or specific drug-exposed tumors (none of must_not_contain present in matched fields).

failure_mode: L4 demographic exclusion: 'acute myeloid leukemia bone marrow' is dominated in corpus by large pediatric AML cohorts (TARGET etc.); the 'adult-only, excluding pediatric/neonatal' constraint is an age-attribute filter that semantic search ignores. Must drop any dataset whose subjects are children/infants.
pass_criteria: top-5 are adult AML bone-marrow scRNA-seq datasets only; no dataset whose cohort is pediatric/childhood/neonatal/infant AML appears (none of must_not_contain in matched metadata).

must_not_contain: cardiovascular disease;coronary artery disease;myocardial infarction;heart failure;atherosclerosis;hypertension;stroke;ischemic heart;cardiac comorbidity
failure_mode: L4 comorbidity exclusion (hardest variant): T2D and cardiovascular disease are heavily co-mentioned in metadata because they are clinically linked, so retrieval surfaces datasets that explicitly include CVD comorbidity. The query demands the OPPOSITE — T2D cohorts where CVD is an exclusion criterion. Negation over a strongly correlated comorbidity term.
pass_criteria: top-5 are T2D pancreatic-islet transcriptomics where subjects have no cardiovascular comorbidity (or CVD is an explicit exclusion criterion); ZERO datasets mention CVD/coronary/MI/heart-failure as a present subject condition.

failure_mode: L4 substance exclusion + lexical trap: 'non-alcoholic' contains the substring 'alcoholic', so token-level BM25 and dense search both pull alcoholic liver disease (ALD) / alcoholic hepatitis datasets to the top. The negation prefix MUST be honored; alcohol-related steatohepatitis cohorts must be excluded even though they share fatty-liver vocabulary.
pass_criteria: top-5 are NAFLD/MASLD/NASH liver RNA-seq with explicitly non-alcoholic etiology; ZERO alcoholic liver disease / alcoholic hepatitis / alcohol-exposure datasets (none of must_not_contain present).

failure_mode: L4 control-only exclusion: most PBMC scRNA-seq datasets in the corpus are disease-vs-healthy case-control studies that mention 'healthy controls' as one arm. The query wants datasets composed ONLY of healthy donors (reference atlases), so a dataset that contains both patients and healthy controls must be EXCLUDED despite matching 'healthy control PBMC scRNA-seq'.
pass_criteria: top-5 are PBMC scRNA-seq datasets consisting solely of healthy/normal donors (reference/baseline); ZERO datasets that also include patient/disease arms (none of must_not_contain in matched description).

must_not_contain: male breast cancer;male patient;men;male subject;male donor;xy karyotype;both sexes;mixed sex
failure_mode: L4 sex-specific exclusion: 'breast cancer' retrieval mostly returns female cohorts but the corpus also has male breast cancer (MBC) and mixed-sex studies; the explicit 'female-only, excluding male' constraint is a subject-sex attribute filter that semantic similarity ignores. Any dataset including male subjects must be dropped.
pass_criteria: top-5 are breast cancer spatial transcriptomics with female-only cohorts; ZERO male breast cancer or mixed-sex datasets appear (none of must_not_contain present in matched metadata).

failure_mode: L1+L5: paired-biofluid same-subject. System historically returns datasets with EITHER CSF OR blood (single-compartment MS studies are abundant) but not the same-subject CSF+blood pair. Pass requires BOTH compartments from the same individuals, not either alone.
pass_criteria: Top results MUST be a single dataset containing BOTH cerebrospinal fluid AND peripheral blood from the SAME subjects (paired/matched), not a CSF-only or blood-only MS dataset. Both UBERON:0001359 and UBERON:0001256 must co-occur in the same study.

failure_mode: L1+L5: paired-biofluid same-subject across two body fluids (saliva + plasma). Dense retrieval tends to anchor on 'proteomics' + 'cancer' and return single-fluid plasma proteomics; the saliva arm gets dropped. Conjunction of two distinct biofluids from the same subject is the trap.
pass_criteria: Top results MUST be a dataset where BOTH saliva (UBERON:0001836) AND blood plasma (UBERON:0001969) are profiled from the SAME patients. A plasma-only or saliva-only proteomics study does NOT satisfy the conjunction.

failure_mode: L1+L5: tumor vs patient-matched adjacent-normal pairing. The trap is that the system returns tumor-only cohorts or unmatched tumor-vs-healthy-donor comparisons; the requirement is the SAME-PATIENT tumor+adjacent-normal pair (a within-subject paired design), which is easily collapsed to a generic tumor RNA-seq hit.
pass_criteria: Top results MUST contain BOTH tumor AND patient-matched adjacent-normal tissue from the SAME individuals. A tumor-only dataset, or tumor compared to unrelated healthy donors, fails the paired conjunction.

failure_mode: L5: three-way organ conjunction (heart AND kidney AND liver) from the SAME donor. This is the hardest cardinality case — the OR-collapse risk multiplies with each added facet, so the system returns single-organ sepsis studies (kidney-only AKI, liver-only) instead of the all-three-organ same-donor design.
pass_criteria: Top results MUST be a dataset profiling ALL THREE organs (heart UBERON:0000948 AND kidney UBERON:0002113 AND liver UBERON:0002107) from the SAME donors. A dataset with only one or two of the three organs fails the multi-AND requirement.

abbrev_under_test: PBMC=peripheral blood mononuclear cell;SLE=systemic lupus erythematosus
failure_mode: L5 (+L2 for PBMC/SLE): tri-modal SAME-SAMPLE conjunction. Requires all three single-cell modalities measured on the SAME cells, not three separate assays on different aliquots. The system tends to return a single-modality scRNA-seq lupus study; the AND across three co-assayed modalities is the trap.
pass_criteria: Top results MUST be a dataset co-assaying ALL THREE modalities (scRNA-seq AND scATAC-seq AND CITE-seq) on the SAME single cells/nuclei. A dataset offering only one or two of these modalities, or three modalities on separate samples, fails the same-sample tri-modal conjunction.

failure_mode: L5 (+L2 for PBC): triple constraint cell-type AND tissue AND disease must ALL hold in one dataset (Treg ∧ liver ∧ PBC). The system relaxes the conjunction — returning blood Tregs, or liver scRNA-seq without the Treg focus, or generic autoimmune-liver studies — instead of the intersection of all three facets.
pass_criteria: Top results MUST satisfy ALL THREE: regulatory T cells (CL:0000815) AND liver tissue (UBERON:0002107) AND primary biliary cholangitis. Blood-derived Tregs, non-Treg liver scRNA-seq, or PBC studies lacking the Treg+liver focus do NOT satisfy the triple conjunction.

failure_mode: L2-adjacent gene+species parsing trap: 'Trp53' is the MOUSE ortholog symbol (human is TP53). System must keep the species-specific gene casing/spelling, bind organism=mouse, and not collapse Trp53->TP53->human. Distinct from existing foxg1a/zebrafish gold (hard_q13).
pass_criteria: top-5 includes >=1 dataset with mouse + Trp53/p53 KO + ATAC-seq + organoid/intestine; results must be mouse (10090), not human TP53 studies

failure_mode: Rare-modality combo trap: 'CUT&RUN' and 'CUT&Tag' contain the ampersand which tokenizers often split/drop, and both can be mis-mapped to generic ChIP-seq. Must keep these as distinct low-frequency modalities rather than coercing to ChIP-seq.
pass_criteria: top-5 includes >=1 dataset explicitly tagged CUT&RUN or CUT&Tag (not plain ChIP-seq) + H3K27me3 + ESC; ampersand modality preserved

failure_mode: Rare-modality trap: 'Perturb-seq' (a.k.a. CROP-seq/CRISPRi screen with scRNA readout) is low-frequency and easily reduced to plain scRNA-seq, dropping the CRISPR-perturbation design. Hyphen+'seq' token also splits poorly.
pass_criteria: top-5 includes >=1 dataset with Perturb-seq / pooled CRISPR + single-cell readout + iPSC neurons; perturbation design not lost

failure_mode: Explicit-healthy-control trap (L5-adjacent conjunction): the 'must include healthy control' constraint is routinely dropped, returning UC-only cohorts. System must require BOTH disease arm AND a healthy/normal control arm in the same study.
pass_criteria: top-5 includes >=1 dataset with UC colonic mucosa AND an explicit healthy/normal control group in the same study; UC-only datasets do not satisfy

failure_mode: Combined trap: (a) British/American spelling 'oesophageal'/'oesophagus'/'tumour' must match US 'esophageal'/'esophagus'/'tumor' indexed corpus; (b) cross-species same-disease requires BOTH human (9606) AND mouse (10090) of the SAME disease, not either alone.
pass_criteria: top-5 includes >=1 human ESCC scRNA-seq AND >=1 mouse esophageal SCC model (or one dataset spanning both); spelling variants oesophagus/tumour resolved

failure_mode: Temporal/longitudinal trap with explicit timepoints (day 0/3/7): system tends to ignore the multi-timepoint sampling constraint and return single-timepoint cross-sectional muscle studies. Must require a true time-course design with >=3 timepoints in the same subjects.
pass_criteria: top-5 includes >=1 dataset with skeletal muscle + exercise + a longitudinal time-course (multiple post-exercise timepoints, ideally day 0/3/7); single-timepoint studies do not satisfy
